concerns.text: T010 and T010a mandate a `FatalError` if real data is missing and `--synthetic` is not set. This silently weakens the Plan.md 'Synthetic Fallback' constraint which requires the pipeline to generate synthetic data for CI validation automatically. The task enforces a hard block (manual intervention) rather than the spec'd automatic fallback, violating the 'Feasibility' and 'Reproducibility' constraints.

T030 instructs the sensitivity analysis to 're-run ingestion parameters' (full re-ingestion of raw satellite data) for each cloud cover threshold. This violates the spec's FR-006/SC-005 which defines sensitivity as a sweep over thresholds applied to *existing* NDVI time-series (filtering/aggregation), not a computationally prohibitive re-ingestion of raw imagery. This semantic drift makes the task infeasible on the target CPU-only runner.

T017b asserts the spatial join must meet the ≥95% threshold or log a warning. This drops the acceptance criterion from the Spec's 'Edge Cases' section which mandates an automatic fallback to 'village-level aggregation' if N < 300. The task lacks the logic to trigger this fallback, meaning the pipeline would fail or halt instead of executing the spec-mandated recovery strategy.

T025 implements regression with Cluster-Robust SEs but fails to ensure `village_id` is derived and present in the `analysis_dataset.csv` (constructed in T018-T021). The Spec requires clustering by village/region; without a task to explicitly retain or aggregate `village_id` in the feature engineering phase, the regression will fail at runtime, violating the functional requirement FR-004.

T018c validates the CSA Index against `contracts/dataset.schema.yaml` (derived schema). The Spec FR-003 requires validating the index against the 'survey data schema' (source definition). This task silently relaxes the verification step, potentially allowing index construction logic to drift from the source data definition, violating the 'Verified Accuracy' constitution principle.
